title: Let the ticket list sort only the way the API says

blocks.text: The helpdesk's ticket list takes its order from the request: `GET /tickets?sort=opened&dir=desc`. The API documents three sort keys, `priority`, `opened` and `title`, and two directions, `asc` and `desc`. The `ticket` table has more columns than that, among them `customer_tier`, which agents must never be able to rank tickets by.

`TicketList.titles(sort, dir)` already builds and runs the query. Write `orderBy(sort, dir)` in `src/main/java/practice/TicketList.java`: the text that goes after `ORDER BY`. A documented request sorts the list; any other request is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException`, and nothing it contains reaches the database. The key `opened` sorts by the column `opened_at`.
About eight lines in total. The tests run against an H2 in-memory database.

cases.says: each documented sort key orders the tickets by its column, ascending or descending
a real column of the table that the API does not document is refused, not sorted by
a direction with anything beyond asc or desc is refused, and nothing in it runs

origin.section: A Bind Parameter Holds a Value, So a Sort Column Comes from an Allow-List

concepts: A sort column or direction can't be a bind parameter, so the code maps each documented sort key to SQL text it wrote itself and refuses anything else; an identifier-shaped check still lets through real columns the API doesn't expose.
